bib.title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation

read.skipped: Reference list and the long qualitative example rows of Tables 9, 11, 12 skimmed only.

question: Can retrieved documents be compressed into a short textual summary, possibly empty, that keeps a frozen LM's end-task performance at a fraction of the prompt tokens?
hypothesis: Compressing retrieved documents with end-task-trained compressors cuts inference cost and removes irrelevant content that distracts the LM, with minimal loss in task performance.
contributions: RECOMP (Retrieve, Compress, Prepend) with an extractive and an abstractive compressor trained on end-task signal from a black-box LM
Selective augmentation: compressor can return an empty string
Evidence that compressors transfer across LMs on language modelling and partly on QA, with a manual faithfulness check

method.summary: A 110M contriever dual encoder (extractive, contrastive loss on sentences scored by the reader LM's likelihood or EM) and a T5-large 775M encoder-decoder (abstractive, distilled from gpt-3.5-turbo summaries filtered by the reader's end-task score, with empty-string targets when retrieval hurts) compress the top 5 retrieved 100-word documents before they are prepended to a frozen LM.
method.task: retrieval-augmented language modelling (WikiText-103) and open-domain QA (NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA)

datasets.name: WikiText-103
datasets.size: extractive train 1,398,318 / val 1,5483 (as printed); abstractive train 38,410 / val 9,603 (from 2% of training set)
datasets.split: train for compressors; dev/test for perplexity
datasets.preprocessing: BM25 top 5 docs, top 20 sentences; sentence split with NLTK; articles containing the input removed from the corpus; retrieval every 32 tokens

datasets.name: Natural Questions
datasets.size: extractive train 42,149 / val 9,769; abstractive train 39,466 / val 4,931
datasets.preprocessing: contriever-msmarco top 5 docs, top 20 sentences, Wikipedia page title prepended to each sentence

datasets.name: TriviaQA
datasets.size: extractive train 70,032 / val 8,753; abstractive train 48,322 / val 5,887

datasets.name: HotpotQA
datasets.size: extractive train 24,526 / val 3,068; abstractive train 26,556 / val 2,937
datasets.split: 500 randomly sampled dev examples for evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: summaries generated only for training data whose gold answer is in retrieved docs (56% of training data) to cut API cost

models.name: Extractive compressor
models.init_from: contriever checkpoint (unsupervised for LM; contriever-msmarco for QA)

models.name: Abstractive compressor
models.init_from: T5-large checkpoint (already trained on summarization data)

other.use: scoring LM for LM compressor training and eval
reader for QA and scoring LM for QA compressors

training.objective: extractive: contrastive loss, -log e^sim(x,p) / (e^sim(x,p)+sum e^sim(x,n)); abstractive: seq2seq fine-tuning on filtered teacher summaries (empty string when prepending the summary scores worse than no retrieval)

other.checkpoint_selection: best reranked perplexity (LM) or best reranked accuracy (QA) on validation set
other.separate_compressors: one extractive and one abstractive trained per dataset
other.teacher_decoding: OpenAI API temperature 0.7, top p = 1; four summaries per example for LM (prompts of Table 8), single prompt per QA dataset; 2% of WikiText train = 48,013 examples
other.filtering: extractive: positives = best-scoring sentence, negatives = up to 5 top-contriever sentences scoring lower by threshold epsilon (epsilon value not given); % filtered per Table 5; abstractive QA drops examples where summary does not improve

inference.samples: inferred: single run per setting; no seeds or repeated runs reported
inference.prompting: 5 randomly sampled training examples as in-context examples (110, 147, 149 tokens avg for NQ, TQA, HotpotQA), no retrieved docs in the examples; retrieved docs concatenated in ascending score order, best closest to the question
inference.retrieval: QA: contriever-msmarco, top 5 100-word docs from Wikipedia Dec 2018; LM: BM25, top 5, retrieval every 32 tokens

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: WikiText-103 perplexity of the LM with the compressed evidence prepended

metrics.name: # tokens
metrics.definition: tokens of in-context evidence, excluding in-context examples

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell, no variance or significance test; faithfulness and comprehensiveness judged manually by the authors on 30 random non-empty summaries per dataset.

availability.data: states code, prompts and API-generated data are released

prompts.purpose: GPT-3.5 summaries for NQ and TQA
prompts.text: Compress the information in the retrieved documents into a 2-sentence summary that could be used to answer the question: Question: query Retrieved documents: docs Compressed documents:
Source documents: docs Question: query Generate a reasoning chain to answer the question:
Generate the next two sentences of the given query using the information from the provided documents.
Select sentences from the retrieved docs that are most likely be in the next sentence.
Generate the next one sentence of the given query using the information from the provided documents
Summarize the information from the provided documents

evidence.quote: using a batch size of 64, learning rate of 2e-5 and 1000 warmup steps for 3 epochs
using a batch size of 16, learning rate of 1e-5 and 1000 warmup steps for 3 epochs

results.claim: On NQ the trained abstractive compressor gives 5% of the tokens for a 2 EM loss versus full top-5 documents.
results.setup: Flan-UL2 20B reader, 5-shot, contriever-msmarco top 5 100-word Wikipedia (Dec 2018) passages, compressors trained per dataset; NQ dev; 36 vs 660 tokens
results.note: Table 2: Ours abstractive 37.04 EM at 36 tokens; top 5 documents 39.39 at 660 tokens
results.quote: On NQ, it achieves a compression ratio of 5% tokens while losing 2 EM points compared to prepending full documents.

results.claim: On TriviaQA the abstractive compressor gives 5% of the tokens for a 3.7 EM loss.
results.setup: Flan-UL2 20B reader, 5-shot, contriever-msmarco top 5 100-word Wikipedia (Dec 2018) passages, compressors trained per dataset; TQA test; 32 vs 677 tokens
results.quote: On TQA, we observe similar trends, compression ratio of 5% tokens while losing 3.7 EM points compared to prepending full sets of documents.

results.claim: On HotpotQA the extractive compressor (two sentences) gives 11% of the tokens for a 2.4 EM loss; abstractive is weaker there.
results.setup: Flan-UL2 20B reader, 5-shot, contriever-msmarco top 5 100-word Wikipedia (Dec 2018) passages, compressors trained per dataset; 500 random HotpotQA dev examples; 75 vs 684 tokens
results.note: Table 2: extractive Ours 30.40 EM, 75 tokens; abstractive Ours 28.20 EM, 64 tokens
results.quote: find extractive approach to be more helpful, achieving 11% compression rate while losing 2.4 EM points compared to prepending full documents.

results.claim: Trained extractive compressor (one sentence) beats BM25, Contriever and NE/BoW on NQ and beats DPR (fine-tuned on NQ) in-domain.
results.setup: Flan-UL2 20B reader, 5-shot, contriever-msmarco top 5 100-word Wikipedia (Dec 2018) passages, compressors trained per dataset; NQ dev, 37 tokens
results.table: Table 2, row Extractive Ours, column NQ EM (36.57); DPR 34.32; Contriever 30.06

results.claim: Off-the-shelf T5 summariser compresses most (7-10 tokens) and gains 4-6 EM over no retrieval.
results.setup: Flan-UL2 20B reader, 5-shot, contriever-msmarco top 5 100-word Wikipedia (Dec 2018) passages, compressors trained per dataset
results.quote: Off-the-shelf summarization model (T5) boasts the highest level of compression, achieving 4-6 points gains in EM while adding mere 7-10 tokens.

results.claim: Oracle compressors beat full documents at 6-13% of tokens; extractive oracle on NQ reaches 60.22 EM with 34 tokens.
results.setup: Flan-UL2 20B reader, 5-shot, contriever-msmarco top 5 100-word Wikipedia (Dec 2018) passages, compressors trained per dataset; NQ; oracle picks best sentence per example using gold answer, so it is an upper bound not a method
results.table: Table 2, row Extractive Oracle, column NQ EM

results.claim: Language modelling: more documents is not better; top-1 document beats top-5 in perplexity on WikiText-103 with GPT-2.
results.setup: GPT-2 117M, BM25 retrieval every 32 tokens, 100-word docs; top 5 truncated to 512 tokens
results.note: Table 1: top 1 = 32.90 (141 tokens); top 5 = 35.53 (512 tokens); no retrieval 37.84
results.quote: prepending top 1 document outperforms prepending top 5 documents.

results.claim: Language modelling: both trained compressors give 25% of top-1 document tokens at minimal perplexity cost, and transfer to GPT2-XL and GPT-J.
results.setup: Compressors trained with GPT-2 as base; evaluated on GPT2-XL 1.5B and GPT-J 6B; WikiText-103
results.quote: Comparing to prepending one document, we achieve a compression ratio of 25% at minimum performance drop.
results.table: Table 1, row Abstractive Ours (init. w/ T5), column GPT2 PPL 33.64 at 15 tokens; extractive Ours 33.67 at 31 tokens

results.claim: On language modelling the abstractive compressor prepends a summary to only 33% of examples (selective augmentation).
results.quote: prepending summaries to only 33% of examples

results.claim: Training-set summaries are empty for 4-24% of examples (Table 5 lists 25% NQ, 16% TQA, 4% HotpotQA, 24% Wikitext).
results.setup: teacher gpt-3.5-turbo summaries filtered by end-task score
results.note: Text says 4-24%; Table 5 % empty column shows NQ 25
results.quote: 4-24% of training examples for abstractive compressors

results.claim: Transfer to LLaMA-13B is partial: on NQ/TQA about 5% tokens with under 5 EM drop, but no clear gain over Contriever on TQA/HotpotQA.
results.setup: Compressors trained for Flan-UL2, applied to LLaMA-13B
results.quote: on NQ/TQA, our compressor obtains 5% compression ratio with less than 5 EM drop compared to full document setting
results.table: Table 10, row Abstractive Ours, column NQ EM 36.32; extractive Ours 34.38; Top 5 37.04

results.claim: Models copy answers from irrelevant evidence: GPT-3.5 summaries lead to 85% wrong copying, ours 39%.
results.setup: NQ dev, Flan-UL2; % of predictions in evidence when gold answer is not in evidence
results.quote: Our compressor successfully reduce such erroneous behavior to 39%.

results.claim: Manual check: GPT-3.5 summaries are more useful than the trained compressor's on all three datasets; HotpotQA is worst (40% useful ours vs 50%).
results.setup: 30 non-empty summaries per dataset, judged by the authors; faithful and comprehensive both needed
results.table: Table 4, row HQA Ours, column % Use. 40; GPT-3.5 50

limits: Compressors are trained per dataset and per reader LM; transfer to LLaMA-13B is worse than in-model and sometimes no better than baselines.

Abstractive compressor is less faithful than its GPT-3.5 teacher and less useful on multi-hop HotpotQA (40% useful vs 50%); the authors say learning an abstractive compressor for complex tasks needs further study.
Extractive compressor uses a fixed number of sentences; adaptive/selective extractive compression is left to future work.
Retriever quality is not studied (retrieved docs assumed given); readers are short-context 2023 LMs; manual evaluation is 30 summaries per dataset by the authors; single runs, no variance reported.
Oracle results use gold answers and are upper bounds, not achievable methods.
Training data depends on gpt-3.5-turbo output, which may include factual errors (ethics statement).

terms.definition: Retrieve, Compress, Prepend: an intermediate step that compresses retrieved documents into a textual summary before in-context augmentation
the compressor returns an empty summary when the retrieved documents are irrelevant or unhelpful
